ceiling_directive: Strengthen prop:nonorbit-exact-pvalue by constructing a computable nuisance-maximized exact p-value for a nondegenerate binary histogram statistic, proving uniform finite-sample validity, and evaluating its rejection regions and power in the balanced 250-of-500 audit.
improvement_directive: Replace the corner-only exact test with a computable nuisance-maximized procedure for a practically relevant binary histogram statistic, and prove its finite-sample validity over every legal weak-null schedule. Apply it to the 250-of-500 audit and compare its rejection behavior with the HC2/robust-t workflow.
critique: The theorems establish the advertised equivalence partitions, maximal common groups, and sharp zero/two/three-unit separator phase diagram within the fixed histogram-profile model; no stated conclusion depends on an open conjecture. The contribution nevertheless concerns a deliberately restricted schedule-universal, histogram-measurable stabilizer rather than exact weak-null tests generally, and its inferential output consists only of coarse orbit ranks plus a corner-event p-value with an exceptionally degenerate rejection event. The DeclareDesign and HC2 discussion therefore remains diagnostic: no usable exact procedure, power calculation, or audit computation demonstrates practical inferential value for the 250-of-500 experiment. This confines the delivered work to a narrow combinatorial classification and prevents the package from reaching the field-tier floor or a leading-journal score above the high-fives. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]
